city_office.name: City of Kitchener corporate sustainability / climate action
city_office.rebate_page_note: Kitchener pages read cover city operations and TransformWR only; no resident rebate or retrofit page found on kitchener.ca. Closest regional page: Region of Waterloo RetrofitWR (https://www.regionofwaterloo.ca/programs-and-services/climate-and-environment/climate-action/retrofit-waterloo-region/), which said GrandBridge loans cover Cambridge and North Dumfries, with free Energy Coach for all Waterloo Region residents (https://retrofitwr.ca/energy-coaching/).

on/kitchener.notes: Best fit is Reep Green Solutions plus the Greater KW Chamber directory; Kitchener has no resident rebate page of its own and RetrofitWR loans are not yet for Kitchener, so a pitch should lean on rebates and installers, not the city program.

city_office.rebate_page_note: City news post (dated June 29, 2026) on RetrofitWR loans up to $40,000 for GrandBridge Energy customers. Also https://cambridge.ca/resident-services/utilities/ (not read). The Environment page itself links to no home retrofit info.

community_groups.name: Reep Green Solutions
community_groups.note: Regional, not Cambridge-based; delivery partner of RetrofitWR per the Region page. Site 403 to fetcher.

news.name: CambridgeToday

on/cambridge.notes: Cambridge is the one city here where the City itself promotes a retrofit program (RetrofitWR), so a rebate and installer page is a natural resource next to it; no Cambridge-only home energy non-profit was found, and RetrofitWR is a loan, not a rebate.

on/peterborough.notes: Best fit is GreenUP's Home Energy page and the City's Better Homes Peterborough page; awkward because Better Homes Peterborough is itself a city-backed program with its own installer list, so frame our page as a neutral rebates and reviews companion.
